title: slayer job
description: A job says how to render a scene: the scene, the film, the time or span, the camera, the development, the titles and sound laid over it, and what comes out.

$schema.description: The name of this schema, which says the document is a slayer job. Always https://github.com/janearc/slayer/schemas/job-v1.json; required.

scene.description: Which scene to render, in exactly one of four forms: set, smoke, named or frames. Required; for example {set: ../sets/moonlake.yaml}.

set.description: A set file, its path relative to this job. For example ../sets/moonlake.yaml.

smoke.description: A numbered smoke scene, counting from 1. For example 3.

named.description: A scene built in Go, by its name; the parameters go in with. A bridge until the scene has a set file; for example fire-night.

with.description: The named scene's parameters, checked by that scene and not by this schema. Only beside named; for example {seed: 7}.

play.description: A cue sheet that plays the named scene's channels from the job's sound, which must be a tune; its path relative to this job. Only beside named; for example zappy-plays.yaml.

frames.description: A directory of frames already rendered, .pfm or .png, taken in name order. Nothing is traced: only development, titles, sound and the film are done.

film.description: The picture's size, rays and lens. Every key is optional; a preset gives a size and sometimes a rate, and a key written beside it stands over it.

preset.description: A named size, and for the previews a rate, from the presets table. For example portrait (1080 by 1920) or video-preview (320 by 180 at 6 frames a second); 720 and 320 may be written bare.

width.description: The picture's width in pixels, from 1 to 8192. Unsaid, it comes from the preset, then the set. For example 1920.

height.description: The picture's height in pixels, from 1 to 8192. Unsaid, it comes from the preset, then the set. For example 1080.

rays.description: Rays along each side of a pixel, from 1 to 16, so 4 is sixteen rays a pixel. Unsaid, the set's count is used.

wide.description: The angle the lens sees across the picture, in degrees, above 0 and below 180. Say wide or tall, not both; for example 55.

tall.description: The angle the lens sees down the picture, in degrees, above 0 and below 180. The way to frame a tall picture; say wide or tall, not both. For example 60.

exposure.description: What one watt a steradian is in the picture's light, above 0. Unsaid, the set's exposure is used; for example 0.5.

aperture.description: How wide the lens is open, across, in the scene's own unit (metres for a set or a smoke), above 0. Things nearer or further than the focus are blurred, more the wider it is; say it beside focus. Unsaid, the lens is a pinhole and everything is sharp. On the gpu only. For example 0.1.

focus.description: How far off the lens is focused, in the scene's own unit (metres for a set or a smoke), above 0 and further than the aperture is wide. Say it beside aperture. For example 12.

mode.description: What the picture shows. light, the default, is the traced light. wire is the edges of every mesh face the first ray of each pixel meets, from the same camera and time, with nothing lit: a surface with no polygons is a flat tint, a height field shows its sample cells, and the sky and volumes are black. wire is drawn on the cpu only; renderer gpu is refused.

renderer.description: Which renderer draws the frames: cpu, gpu, gpu-native-shadows or gpu-native. Unsaid, the command line or the set decides.

quality.description: exact draws every frame in full; preview draws a quicker, rougher frame for looking. The default is exact.

vibes.description: For films to watch, not to measure: turns every shortcut on. A flag: fastlight and a shortcut's own word stand over it. Refused with whatever a shortcut it turns on is refused with.

fastlight.description: Fast light: turns the light shortcuts on, each an approximation. A flag: a shortcut's own word stands over it. Refused on the cpu, through a rig's lens, for a named scene, and beside a proof.

shortcuts.description: The parts of a quicker picture, each on or off by name, standing over fastlight and vibes. Each is an approximation, and a picture drawn with one says so.

lamp-store.description: Mist and smoke lit from a store of each lamp's light, once a frame. A shadow cast into mist goes as soft as a cell of the store. Refused with more than eight lamps, beside volume-lighting: cached, and as fastlight is.

sky-looks.description: The sky's sixteen looks from a surface shared among a pixel's rays. Each ray takes its share, not all sixteen, so sky-lit shade is a little rougher within a pixel. Refused without lamp-store, and as fastlight is.

camera.description: The camera: {name: NAME} for one the scene defines, or a path of moves as a sequence plan writes one. A zoom may stand beside a name.

name.description: A camera the scene defines, by its name. Not beside look-at, up, moves or unit; for example rim.

unit.description: The unit of the path's points, which must be the scene's own: m, metres, for sets and smokes; a named scene's unit as the scene names it, for example a thousand kilometres. The renderer checks it against the scene. Required with a path.

look-at.description: The point the camera looks at, unless a move says its own look. Required with a path; for example {x: 0, y: 1, z: 0}.

up.description: Which way is up for the camera. The default is {x: 0, y: 1, z: 0}, the scene's up.

moves.description: The camera's moves, in order, each starting where the last ended. Required with a path; from 1 to 1024 moves.

zoom.description: A change of the lens's angle across the picture over time, without moving the camera. For example {from: {value: 60, unit: deg}, to: {value: 20, unit: deg}, duration: {value: 8, unit: s}}.

at.description: A still: the scene's time when the picture is taken, in seconds from 0 to 86400. Not beside fps or duration; for example {value: 20, unit: s}.

fps.description: A film: frames a second, from 1 to 120. Unsaid, a preset's rate is used; for example 24.

duration.description: A film: how long it plays, in seconds, from 0.001 to 3600. Required for a film; for example {value: 10, unit: s}.

start.description: A film: the scene's time at the first frame, in seconds from 0 to 86400. The default is 0; for example {value: 40, unit: s}.

scene-duration.description: A film: how much scene time the film spans, stretched over its duration, in seconds from 0.001 to 86400. Unsaid, scene time runs with the film; {value: 3600, unit: s} over 30 seconds is an hour in half a minute.

shutter.description: Motion blur: each frame is drawn glimpses times across the part of its interval the angle leaves open, and the light averaged. Films only; absent, a frame is one instant.

angle.description: How much of each frame's interval the shutter is open, in degrees above 0 and up to 360; 180 is half. For example {value: 180, unit: deg}.

value.description: The angle in degrees, above 0 and up to 360.

glimpses.description: How many times each frame is drawn while the shutter is open, from 1 to 64. A frame costs this many renders; for example 4.

print.description: Plain development: the tone curve from light to picture. Not beside stock; with neither, the scene's own print is used.

knee.description: Where the curve's shoulder starts, as a share of white, from 0 up to but not 1. Required; for example 0.7.

top.description: The brightest light the print holds, in whites, above 1; it lands on white. Required; for example 8.

bloom.description: How far bright light spreads into its neighbours, from 0 to 20 pixels. The default is 0, none; for example 2.

stops.description: Exposure given at the print, in stops from -40 to 40; each stop doubles the light. A raw through a set's lens rig is in joules and sits far under white: moonlake's prints at 23. The default is 0; for example -1.

stock.description: Development through a ninjafilm stock, with its grain and curve. Not beside print; for example {name: dusk, seed: 7}.

name.description: The stock, one of the shelf: soot, ash, smoke, dusk, pollen or lantern. Required.

seed.description: Fixes the grain, so the same seed lays the same grain. A whole number from 0 to 4294967295; the default is 0.

rated.description: Push or pull, in stops from -6 to 6: the stock developed as if it were that much faster or slower. The default is 0; for example 1.

titles.description: Words, frames and bars drawn over the frames, as a set's hud writes them. For example {rows: 24, elements: {name: {kind: text, words: Moonlake, ink: ink, across: 0.5, down: 0.9}}}.

theme.description: A colourway file the elements' roles come from, its path relative to this job. Unsaid, the hud's own default theme is used.

rows.description: How many rows of cells the picture is laid out in, from 2 to 500; fewer rows is larger type. Unsaid, the hud's default.

elements.description: The elements, each by a name of your choosing, drawn in the order written, each over the ones before.

sound.description: The soundtrack: {tune, voicing} for music rendered here, or {file, from, score} for an audio file. Cut at the film's end; silence after shorter sound.

tune.description: The score of music rendered here, a path relative to this job or @name for a built-in. Needs voicing; for example ../improv/moonlake/score.yaml.

voicing.description: What plays the tune's parts, a path relative to this job or @name for a built-in. Needs tune; for example @plain.

file.description: An audio file, its path relative to this job. Not beside tune; for example ../music/take.wav.

from.description: Where in the audio file the film's sound starts, in seconds from 0 to 86400. The default is 0; for example {value: 12.5, unit: s}.

score.description: A score file giving the audio file's beats, its path relative to this job. Unsaid, the beats are estimated and said to be.

outputs.description: What is written, by role, each a path relative to this job. A still writes picture or raw; a film writes frames, movie or both. With none, the verb's default place is used.

picture.description: A still's picture, a .png. For example ../renders/moonlake.png.

raw.description: A still's light before development, a .pfm, so it can be developed again. For example ../renders/moonlake.pfm.

frames.description: A film's directory of numbered pictures. For example ../renders/moonlake-frames.

movie.description: The film as an .mp4, with its sound. For example ../renders/moonlake.mp4.

note.description: One plain line saying what this render is, shown on its card on the renders page. No tab and no line break. For example: the lake at dusk, first try.

limits.description: Memory and time ceilings, read by the queue only; they never change the picture. For example {memory: {value: 16, unit: GiB}}.

memory.description: The most memory the job may use, in GiB above 0 and up to 1024. For example {value: 16, unit: GiB}.

value.description: The memory in GiB, above 0 and up to 1024.

time.description: The longest the job may run, in seconds above 0 and up to 604800, a week. For example {value: 7200, unit: s}.

value.description: The time in seconds, above 0 and up to 604800.
The time in seconds, from 0 to 86400, a day.
The span in seconds, from 0.001 to 3600, an hour.
The span in seconds, from 0.001 to 86400, a day.
The span in seconds, above 0 and up to 3600, an hour.

x.description: Metres east of the scene's origin.

y.description: Metres up from the scene's origin.

z.description: Metres south of the scene's origin.

from.description: Where the move starts, which is where the last one ended. For example {x: 0, y: 2, z: 10}.

to.description: Where the move ends; the same point as from makes a hold. For example {x: 0, y: 2, z: 4}.

speed.description: Travel at a constant speed, in metres a second. Say speed or duration, not both; for example {value: 2, unit: m/s}.

value.description: The speed in metres a second, above 0.

duration.description: Travel over this many seconds of scene time. Say speed or duration, not both; for example {value: 4, unit: s}.

ease.description: linear moves at one pace; smooth starts and ends gently and needs a duration. The default is linear.

look.description: The move's own look: the point it looks at as it starts and as it ends, eased as the move is. A hold that looks from one point to another is a pan.

from.description: What the camera looks at as the move starts.

to.description: What the camera looks at as the move ends.

value.description: The angle across the picture in degrees, above 0 and below 180.

from.description: The lens's angle across the picture as the zoom starts. For example {value: 60, unit: deg}.

to.description: The lens's angle across the picture as the zoom ends. For example {value: 20, unit: deg}.

duration.description: How long the zoom takes, in seconds of scene time from the camera's start. For example {value: 8, unit: s}.

ease.description: linear changes the angle at one pace; smooth starts and ends gently. The default is linear.

to.description: The value it reaches over seconds after start.

start.description: When it starts to change, in seconds of film time. The default is 0.

over.description: How many seconds it takes to change. The default is 0, at once.

kind.description: What the element is: text, a frame or a bar. Required.

words.description: What a text says. A text says words or a count, one of them; for example Moonlake.

count.description: A number a text writes out by its format, alone or as {from, to, start, over} to count across the film. Needs format.

format.description: How a text writes its count, as Go's fmt writes a float64. For example %.0f m.

value.description: How full a bar is, from 0 to 1, alone or as {from, to, start, over}. Required for a bar.

left.description: A frame's or bar's left edge, as a share of the picture's width from 0 to 1.

top.description: A frame's or bar's top edge, as a share of the picture's height from 0 to 1.

right.description: A frame's or bar's right edge, as a share of the picture's width from 0 to 1.

bottom.description: A frame's or bar's bottom edge, as a share of the picture's height from 0 to 1.

across.description: Where a text stands across the picture, as a share of its width from 0 to 1. For example 0.5, the middle.

down.description: Where a text stands down the picture, as a share of its height from 0 to 1. For example 0.9, near the foot.

align.description: How a text sits on its place: left, centre or right. The default is left.

ink.description: The theme's role a text or a frame is drawn in. For example ink.

ground.description: The theme's role behind a text's words. Unsaid, the words stand on the picture.

fill.description: The theme's role a bar's full part is drawn in. For example ok.

empty.description: The theme's role a bar's empty part is drawn in. For example dim.

from.description: When the element appears, in seconds of film time. Unsaid, from the first frame; for example {value: 2, unit: s}.

until.description: When the element goes, in seconds of film time, after from. Unsaid, to the last frame; for example {value: 6, unit: s}.
